General notes: • The Washington Group Questions (WGQ) Short Set are 6 questions designed to identify people with disabilities. Its major objective is to provide information on disability status that is comparable worldwide. • The WGQ should always be used in conjunction with other measurement tools and should not be used in isolation, because it is intended as a screening tool only. • The WGQ is not suitable for children under the age of 5. For this reason, UNICEF and the WG developed the Child Functioning Module (CFM) which is designed to better identify all children with disability. • The WGQ should not to be used as a tool to identify type of impairment; it is not designed for this purpose. It is only meant to identify a person with a disability. Guidance note on using the WGQ: • Ask the WGQ to each HH member individually. • Adopt a neutral attitude; avoid using the word disability during the interview. • Do not pre-select people. E.g. you don’t ask first ‘do you have a disability yes/or no?‘ before using the WQG. This might cause an underestimation of prevalence. • Do not change any question or wording! Always use the same wording and all response categories. • Always ask all WG-questions and answer options, regardless of the situation (even though it might seem repetitive). • Respect the answer given by the respondent; it is not up to the enumerator to judge. Guidance on analysing the data: • If a person responds “Yes, a lot of difficulty” or “Cannot do at all” to ONE of the 6 questions, they need to be considered a person with disability. • Everyone else is regarded as a person without disability.
